sections.1:
This Solution Blueprint establishes the foundation for Apollo Hospital’s RapidResponse implementation and defines the operating model required to support Apollo Hospital’s healthcare supply chain planning needs. The document is intended to capture the business requirements, user stories, analytics, and solution design that will guide configuration for this release, with sufficient technical detail to enable the implementation team to translate Apollo Hospital’s planning intent into an executable solution.

Apollo Hospital’s current planning environment is based on manual processes supported by a legacy HIS landscape, while its planning ambition and maturity are aligned to advanced, fully integrated planning. This creates a clear need for a structured planning platform that can support coordinated decision-making, consistent analytics, and scalable planning execution across Apollo Hospital’s supply chain planning processes. The blueprint therefore focuses on defining how RapidResponse will support Apollo Hospital’s business requirements, improve planning visibility, and enable a more integrated planning operating model.

The solution for Apollo Hospital will be documented through functional requirements, user stories, analytics, resources utilized, and solution design decisions. During development, this blueprint will be updated to reflect approved requirement changes and design refinements so that, at technical go-live, it provides a consolidated view of both Apollo Hospital’s requirements and the implemented solution. Test results are outside the scope of this section and are not included in this document.

Bristlecone will support Apollo Hospital as the system integrator by helping convert Apollo Hospital’s agreed planning requirements into configured capabilities within RapidResponse. The implementation approach will use the blueprint as the authoritative reference for scope, design alignment, and configuration direction, ensuring that Apollo Hospital’s planning processes are represented consistently throughout build, validation, and deployment activities.

The expected outcome for Apollo Hospital is a documented and implementable planning solution that supports advanced, integrated supply chain planning, improves the usability and consistency of planning execution, and provides a controlled basis for future planning enhancements. Where Apollo Hospital-specific details are not yet available in the source documents, they will be confirmed during the implementation phase and incorporated into the blueprint through the defined project governance process.
sections.1.1:
Apollo Hospital operates in the Healthcare industry and is the client organization for this Blueprint. The current enterprise systems landscape for Apollo Hospital is identified as Manual + Legacy HIS, which indicates that planning execution and operational coordination are supported through a combination of manual processes and legacy hospital information system capabilities. Apollo Hospital’s planning maturity is identified as advanced and fully integrated planning, and the solution approach must therefore preserve existing planning discipline while improving data consistency, process orchestration, and decision support across the healthcare planning environment.

For Apollo Hospital, the Blueprint must address the transition from manual and legacy HIS-dependent planning activities toward a more structured, integrated planning capability. The available Apollo Hospital source context does not provide confirmed details for site count, facility hierarchy, geographic footprint, product or service portfolio, user volumes, licensing position, or detailed application architecture; therefore, these items are recorded as . Any design assumptions for Apollo Hospital should be validated during implementation through confirmed data availability, responsibility ownership, and planning process alignment.

The solution for Apollo Hospital is expected to support integrated planning outcomes across demand, supply, inventory, and operational decision-making in a healthcare context. The implementation should focus on establishing reliable planning data inputs, clear planning responsibilities, and standardized collaboration mechanisms so that Apollo Hospital can improve visibility, reduce manual effort, and strengthen end-to-end planning governance. Data requirements such as demand history, annual plan targets, supply lead time history, and a responsibility matrix are relevant planning inputs that Apollo Hospital will need to confirm or provide where applicable.

The intended outcome for Apollo Hospital is a planning environment that supports faster, more consistent decision-making and improves the ability to manage supply chain risks in healthcare operations. By moving from fragmented manual and legacy HIS-supported processes toward an integrated planning model, Apollo Hospital can improve planner productivity, enhance scenario evaluation, and support more coordinated execution across planning functions. Detailed benefits, metrics, and confirmed scope elements for Apollo Hospital will depend on the data, process, and organizational information made available during the Blueprint and implementation phases.
sections.1.2: Mahindra’s current business state is defined by fragmented planning tools and processes, where manual methods and legacy HIS systems restrict end-to-end visibility and coordinated supply chain planning. The lack of integration between business units leads to inconsistent planning outcomes and suboptimal inventory management. Key pain points include poor inventory planning, process inefficiencies, and limited ability to simulate supply chain scenarios or respond rapidly to market changes. These challenges have resulted in excess inventory, stockouts, and missed opportunities for operational optimization.
sections.1.3:
The purpose of this document is to define the Customer Solution blueprint for Mahindra. The blueprint prescribes the scope of processes, capabilities, and resources that will support the RapidStart deployment of Kinaxis RapidResponse for supply management.

The aims of the blueprint are twofold:

Set the baseline for Mahindra’s future-state process and advanced planning capabilities, enabling business and IT teams to adopt a common terminology and understanding of RapidResponse planning paradigms and foundational capabilities.

Ensure a common understanding of the solution scope for the RapidStart deployment phase, providing a complete walk-through of the prescribed processes, resources, and algorithms that comprise the initial implementation.
sections.1.4: The scope of this Blueprint is limited to supply management processes within Mahindra’s supply chain operations for Phase 1 of the Kinaxis RapidResponse implementation. This includes the assessment and redesign of supply planning workflows, integration with existing manual and legacy HIS systems, and the establishment of foundational data and process standards. Demand planning, inventory optimization, and other advanced planning capabilities are out of scope for this phase and will be addressed in subsequent project stages. Any requirements outside the defined scope will be managed through formal change request procedures.

sections.2:
Apollo Hospital will benefit from an intuitive and advanced User Interface for Supply Chain Management and Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP), reducing planner workload through fewer clicks, adaptive functions, and improved user friendliness.

Scenario planning and what-if analysis capabilities will empower Apollo Hospital to drive better decision making and proactively manage supply chain risks.

Sophisticated algorithms embedded in the solution will provide Apollo Hospital with greater control and flexibility to derive expected planning results, including advanced supply allocation and prioritisation based on factors such as demand due date, priority, target, and sourcing rules.

Safety stock recommendations will be dynamically calculated at all inventory levels, from finished goods at the warehouse to purchased raw materials, supporting just-in-time planning and minimising excess and obsolete inventory.

The solution will enable more accurate ‘Available Date’ calculations, improving customer service and order fulfillment reliability.

Key person dependency will be eliminated, with business unit ownership of the solution, standardisation across units, and enhanced staff flexibility through easy role switching.

Data integration will be streamlined, supporting faster onboarding and improved data quality.

Future advanced capabilities, such as demand sensing, multi-echelon inventory optimisation, and AI-driven supply planning, will further enhance forecast accuracy and inventory optimisation across all nodes of Apollo Hospital’s supply chain.

Quantitative benefits for Apollo Hospital include:

Improved customer service by over 25%

Reduction in excess and obsolete inventory by 15–25%

Improved resource efficiency by 10–20%

Planning cycle time reduction by 25–35%

Inventory and carrying cost savings by 10–30%

Reduction in premium freight cost by 15–25%
sections.2.1:
Fragmented Planning Tools and Processes

Mahindra’s reliance on manual methods and legacy HIS systems has resulted in siloed planning, limiting end-to-end visibility and coordinated decision-making.

The coexistence of multiple tools (manual, legacy, Excel) creates inconsistencies and inefficiencies across business units.

Inventory Planning Inefficiencies

Poor inventory planning has led to excess, obsolete, and expiring inventory, increasing holding costs and reducing asset productivity.

Inability to accurately model inventory policies and targets results in frequent deviations from plan.

Scenario Planning and Responsiveness Limitations

Limited ability to simulate supply chain scenarios restricts Mahindra’s responsiveness to market changes and supply disruptions.

Scenario modeling and collaboration are hampered by lack of integrated tools and standardized processes.

Talent and Regional Standardization Risks

Siloed systems and non-standardized processes increase dependency on local expertise, posing risks to talent retention and knowledge transfer.

Regional variations in planning approaches hinder the adoption of best practices and enterprise-wide process harmonization.

sections.3.5:
Mahindra’s Inventory Management Foundation within the Kinaxis RapidResponse implementation is designed to address the company’s key pain point of poor inventory planning, which is exacerbated by partially automated, siloed systems and a mix of manual and legacy HIS ERP environments. The solution establishes a robust, exception-driven foundation for inventory visibility, policy standardization, and proactive management across Mahindra’s automobile supply chain.

Model Inventory Policies and ABC Analysis

Inventory policies are modelled at both part and site levels, supporting ABC classification to prioritize inventory management efforts and optimize working capital.

Safety stock policies are standardized using rules such as FixedLeadTimeSoft, with the ability to override recommendations based on Mahindra’s operational realities.

Min/Max and cycle stock parameters are configured to align with Mahindra’s distribution network, considering transfer costs, transit times, and transportation modes.

Safety Stock and Inventory Quality Management

Safety stock levels are calculated and reviewed using historical demand, service level targets (e.g., 95%), and demand variability.

The Inventory Planning workbook enables Mahindra planners to review, adjust, and override safety stock recommendations, ensuring alignment with service objectives and supply variability.

Inventory Quality Ratio metrics are tracked to assess the health of inventory, supporting continuous improvement.

Inventory Exception Management and Alerting

Exception management capabilities identify inventory exceptions such as stockouts, excess, obsolete, and slow-moving stock at both part and site levels.

The system provides alerting and metric logic for inventory exceptions, order issues within the planning horizon, projected lead time exceptions, and periods of supply below target.

Exception resolution workflows enable Mahindra planners to simulate adjustment options, analyze impacts, and collaborate on corrective actions.

Inventory Visibility and Projections

Mahindra gains end-to-end inventory visibility, including inventory balances, projected inventory positions, and period ending inventory values across the distribution network.

The solution supports demand and inventory visibility at both aggregate and detailed levels, enabling proactive management of inventory positions and transfer requirements.

Excess and Obsolete Reporting

Automated reporting identifies excess and obsolete inventory, supporting Mahindra’s efforts to minimize working capital tied up in non-performing stock.

Inventory projections and turns are monitored to drive timely disposition and replenishment decisions.

Inventory Transfer and Ad-Hoc Management

The Inventory Transfer Workbook enables planners to manage inventory transfers, considering transfer cost, transit time, and transportation mode.

Ad-hoc inventory transfers are supported to address urgent supply imbalances or demand surges within Mahindra’s network.

Integration and Closed Loop Process

Inventory management processes are integrated with supply planning, order management, and distribution planning, ensuring a closed-loop approach.

Adjustments and exception resolutions are captured and, where appropriate, fed back into Mahindra’s ERP systems for execution.

sections.4:
Mahindra’s Demand Planning capability within the Kinaxis RapidResponse implementation is designed to establish a robust, collaborative, and exception-driven process for generating and managing demand forecasts across the automobile business. The solution addresses Mahindra’s current challenges of poor inventory planning, which are compounded by partially automated and siloed legacy systems, by enabling a structured and transparent demand planning process.

Key functional requirements for Mahindra include the ability to define demand planner ownership, establish a demand planning process calendar with clear ownership and cadence, and support both statistical and consensus forecasting. The solution enables the definition and adjustment of statistical forecast parameters, outlier detection, and the assignment of NPI/EOL profiles. Additionally, Mahindra’s planners will be able to review and validate sales history, adjust for outliers and causals, and manage phase-in/phase-out scenarios for products.

The Demand Planning process is further enhanced by the ability to input and adjust forecast categories, disaggregate forecasts, compare current and previous cycles, and visualize key metrics through dashboards and scorecards. This comprehensive approach ensures that Mahindra can generate accurate, consensus-driven demand plans that align with business objectives and support improved supply and inventory planning outcomes.
sections.4.1:
The Demand Planning Process at Mahindra is structured to generate, evaluate, and form consensus around a monthly demand plan for a defined planning horizon, typically spanning 18-24 months. The process begins with data preparation, where demand planners define forecast items at the required aggregation level and cleanse historical data to ensure accuracy. This includes addressing periods with no actuals, adjusting for causals such as promotions, and managing outliers.

Following data preparation, statistical forecasts are generated using configurable parameters and models. Demand planners can assign NPI/EOL profiles and phase-in/phase-out histories to forecast items, ensuring that new and retiring products are accurately represented in the forecast. External forecasts, such as customer or manual forecasts, can be uploaded and reviewed by selecting the appropriate forecast category, providing a comprehensive view of all demand signals.

The consensus demand planning step involves collaborative review and adjustment of the system-generated demand plan by demand planners, product managers, and business managers. Adjustments and overrides are made as necessary, and the final consensus demand plan is approved and published for use by supply planners. This process is supported by regular demand review meetings, where aggregated unconstrained demand plans are aligned with business objectives, risks and opportunities are assessed, and recommendations are formulated for subsequent supply review and S&OP cycles.

Throughout the process, Mahindra’s demand planners leverage dashboards and scorecards for visualization of key metrics, enabling informed decision-making and continuous improvement of forecast accuracy.
sections.4.2.1:
Solution assumptions for Mahindra’s forecast consumption process are as follows:

Only one forecast item can be defined per part-customer record within the system, which may limit the granularity of forecast consumption in cases where multiple demand streams exist for a single part-customer combination.

Forecast items should have a minimum of 24 periods of sales history to generate a valid statistical forecast. Insufficient history may impact the reliability of forecast consumption and the effectiveness of statistical models.

The determination and adjustment of forecast item hierarchies and grouping approaches are critical and must be managed carefully. Significant changes to these structures will require a redesign of statistical parameters and may affect forecast consumption logic.

The ability to exclude forecast items from statistical forecast generation is supported, but the rationale and business rules for such exclusions must be clearly documented and maintained.

Dependencies exist on the quality and completeness of historical sales data, as well as the timely integration of actual demand signals from Mahindra’s manual and legacy HIS ERP systems.

Any additional information, decisions, limitations, exclusions, or dependencies related to forecast consumption will be further clarified during detailed design workshops with Mahindra stakeholders.
sections.4.2.2:
The following resources support Mahindra’s forecast consumption process:

Forecast Consumption Analysis Workbook: Central tool for tracking forecast consumption intervals, analyzing periods of supply, and reviewing forecast spreading profiles.

Review and Adjust Demand Task Flow: Enables planners to review forecast consumption details and adjust demand order information as needed.

Demand Planner Dashboard: Provides planners with a consolidated view of demand metrics, forecast consumption status, and exception alerts.

Demand Order Analysis – Partial Orders Workbook: Supports detailed analysis of demand orders, including partial order consumption and exception identification.

Collaboration Task Flows: Facilitate communication and resolution of exceptions among demand planners.

These resources are designed to provide Mahindra’s planning team with the visibility, analytical tools, and collaborative workflows necessary to optimize forecast consumption and support improved demand planning outcomes.
sections.5:
Supply and Inventory Planning at Apollo Hospital is designed to ensure that supply aligns with demand forecasts, inventory targets are maintained, and operational constraints are respected across the healthcare supply chain. The planning process supports the procurement, management, and distribution of critical medical products and supplies, leveraging advanced, fully integrated planning capabilities. 

Key functional requirements include the ability to assign responsibility for parts to Supply, Master, and Production Planners, manage part lifecycle and supply stages, and configure forecast spreading profiles. The solution enables planners to view, adjust, and simulate changes to a comprehensive set of planning parameters, such as safety stocks, planning calendars, forecast consumption intervals, periods of supply, planning zones (firm, scheduling, and planning), and minimum/maximum stock levels. 

Apollo Hospital’s planners are empowered to manage part source selection, including supply order policies, lead times, and priorities, as well as to collaborate across roles to resolve supply and inventory exceptions. The planning process provides visibility into demand and supply plans by zone, supports exception-based management, and enables simulation of alternative solutions to address constraints and exceptions. This approach ensures that Apollo Hospital can maintain high service levels, minimize stockouts, and optimize inventory across its healthcare network.
sections.5.1:
Review and Adjust Planning Parameters is a foundational process within Apollo Hospital’s supply planning framework. This process enables supply planners to systematically review and maintain the planning parameters that directly impact the generation and execution of the supply plan. Key parameters include planning calendars, sourcing properties (such as order policies, lot sizes, and lead times), safety stock policies, days of supply, and Bill of Materials (BOM) configurations.

Planners begin by reviewing the planning calendars assigned to each part, ensuring that supply plans are generated in accordance with operational schedules and site-specific constraints. Sourcing properties are then evaluated, with the ability to simulate changes to order quantities, lot sizes, planning time fences, and lead times. This simulation capability allows Apollo Hospital to identify high-impact opportunities for lead time reduction and supply chain efficiency improvements.

Safety stock policies and days of supply are also reviewed and adjusted as needed to balance service level objectives with inventory investment. Planners can simulate the impact of policy changes on inventory levels and financial targets, ensuring that adjustments support Apollo Hospital’s broader operational goals. BOM structures are reviewed for accuracy and completeness, with the ability to simulate changes and analyze their downstream impact on supply and production plans.

Throughout the process, planners collaborate with stakeholders to resolve exceptions and determine whether parameter changes should be updated in the RapidResponse planning solution or in Apollo Hospital’s legacy HIS/ERP system. This ensures data integrity and alignment across all planning and execution systems.
sections.5.2:
Managing capacity constraints is a critical component of Apollo Hospital’s supply planning solution. The system provides the ability to define, adjust, and simulate changes to various types of constraints, including production, supplier, and logistics capacities. Planners can set preplan limits, define available capacity for each constraint, and identify key constraints that have the greatest impact on the supply plan.

The Constraint Manager workbook enables planners to review constraint loads, identify periods of overload or underload, and analyze the impact of constraints on the supply plan and master production schedule. Planners can simulate changes to constraint properties, such as adjusting capacity rates, changing constraint types (e.g., from “Load Only” to “Constrained”), and reassigning part-sources to different constraints. The solution supports the use of alternate part-sources and the maintenance of additional constraint variables to resolve capacity issues.

Collaboration tools facilitate the resolution of constraint exceptions, allowing planners to work together to identify and implement the most effective solutions. All changes to constraints are reviewed for their impact on key corporate metrics, and planners can manually update the legacy HIS or ERP system to ensure that constraint changes are reflected in execution systems.

sections.6:
This section outlines the data integration approach for the Kinaxis RapidResponse implementation at Apollo Hospital. The integration framework is designed to ensure secure, reliable, and timely data exchange between Apollo Hospital’s source systems—including manual and legacy Hospital Information Systems (HIS)—and the Kinaxis RapidResponse platform. 

The integration architecture leverages a combination of file-based data extracts, secure file transfer protocols, and transformation processes to facilitate the movement of planning-relevant data. Data flows from Apollo Hospital’s ERP and HIS environments through a secure transfer layer to the RapidResponse environment, where it is validated and loaded for planning and analytics. The integration approach supports both inbound and outbound data flows, enabling closed-loop planning and reporting capabilities.

All data transformation logic is primarily contained within the extract programs developed and maintained by Apollo Hospital IT. The integration process is designed to accommodate Apollo Hospital’s advanced, fully integrated planning maturity, ensuring that data is consistently synchronized between operational systems and the planning platform.
sections.6.1:
The integration architecture for Apollo Hospital’s Kinaxis RapidResponse solution is structured to ensure secure, efficient, and auditable data transfer between Apollo Hospital’s source systems and the RapidResponse platform. The architecture comprises the following key components:

1. **Source Systems (Apollo Hospital Network):** Data originates from Apollo Hospital’s manual and legacy HIS environments. Extract programs developed by Apollo Hospital IT generate flat, tab-delimited ASCII text files containing the required planning, supply, and inventory data.

2. **Data Transfer Layer:** Extracted data files are transmitted from Apollo Hospital’s network to the Kinaxis environment using either the Kinaxis Data Transfer Client (DTC) or an SFTP process. The DTC is installed within Apollo Hospital’s network and is responsible for securely transferring files across the internet, traversing multiple firewalls and perimeter security layers.

3. **Kinaxis Hosted Environment:** Upon arrival, files are received in a secure SFTP location within the Kinaxis RapidResponse Data Center. The files undergo a series of validation checks, including file-level and checksum verification, syntax checking, referential integrity validation, and record-level verification. Only validated data is loaded into the RapidResponse database.

4. **Outbound Data Flows:** Where required, data can be extracted from RapidResponse and transferred back to Apollo Hospital’s network or to external reporting tools, following similar secure transfer protocols.

This architecture ensures that Apollo Hospital’s sensitive healthcare data is protected throughout the integration process, while also supporting the operational and analytical needs of the organization’s advanced planning functions.
sections.6.2:
Apollo Hospital’s Kinaxis RapidResponse solution integrates data from a range of internal systems, primarily the legacy Hospital Information System (HIS) and manual ERP processes. The following categories of data sources are included in the integration scope:

- **Master Data:** Includes materials, customers, suppliers, work centers, bills of material, routings, and calendars. These are primarily sourced from the legacy HIS and manual ERP records.
- **Transactional Data:** Encompasses sales orders, purchase orders, production orders, inventory movements, and batch records. These are extracted from operational modules within the legacy HIS and supporting manual processes.
- **Reference Data:** Covers exchange rates, unit of measure conversions, and other supporting datasets required for planning calculations.

Where applicable, data from ancillary systems or external sources (such as telemetry or third-party logistics providers) may also be integrated to enhance planning accuracy. The specific data sources and their update frequencies are detailed in Section 6.4.

sections.6.4:
The frequency of data integration processes for Apollo Hospital’s Kinaxis RapidResponse implementation is determined by business requirements, planning cycles, and the nature of the data being exchanged. The following table summarizes the typical data feed frequencies for key data categories:

| Data Category         | Source System         | Target System      | Frequency           | Processing Mode      |
|----------------------|----------------------|--------------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Master Data          | Legacy HIS / Manual  | RapidResponse      | Daily / Real-time   | Batch / Real-time   |
| Transactional Data   | Legacy HIS           | RapidResponse      | Daily / Real-time   | Batch / Real-time   |
| Reference Data       | Legacy HIS / Manual  | RapidResponse      | As needed / Daily   | Batch               |
| Telemetry Data       | External Systems     | RapidResponse      | Daily / Real-time   | Batch / Real-time   |
| Outbound Reporting   | RapidResponse        | Power BI           | Daily / Real-time   | Batch / Real-time   |

The integration schedule is designed to ensure that planning data is refreshed in alignment with Apollo Hospital’s operational and planning cycles. Master and transactional data are typically updated at least daily, with real-time updates enabled for critical data flows where required. Reference data updates are scheduled based on business needs, while outbound reporting interfaces are aligned with reporting and analytics requirements.

Any deviations from the standard frequency or additional requirements will be documented and agreed upon during the implementation phase.
